skill.displayName: ClawQuest: Agent Mine - OpenClaw Managed Mining

version.changelog:
No user-facing changes in this version.

- Version bump only; no updates to code or documentation detected.

llm.summary: This skill matches its mining-automation purpose, but it exposes saved game API codes and resource-spending actions through an under-protected local HTTP service.

dimensions.detail: The Express service exposes POST /tool/:name without authentication or authorization and listens without an explicit loopback bind, which is disproportionate for credential and account-control operations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package has a simple npm start script and registry dependencies with lockfile integrity entries; dependency freshness and semver ranges are maintenance risks but not the main security concern.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructions are mostly scoped to using documented tool endpoints; the scanner's self-modification concern appears to be a false positive because the text tells agents not to edit the skill source.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: apiCode values are persisted as plaintext JSON, can be returned in full by get_api_code, and session identifiers are retained in status/event data; this is high-impact credential/session handling with weak containment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Managed mining, stamina purchase, and upstream OpenClaw API calls are purpose-aligned, but the capability includes reusable account API codes, long-running automation, and diamond-spending actions without strong control boundaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only run this service on a trusted local machine or behind strong authentication, treat apiCode as an account secret, avoid shared cache keys such as default, and do not enable auto-buy unless you accept automatic diamond spending. Rotate any apiCode that may have been stored or exposed by this service.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as material: the artifact has one unauthenticated tool route for credential, mining, stop/restart, and stamina-purchase operations, and no per-user authorization around cacheKey or session state.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as material: set_api_code stores reusable apiCode values on disk, and get_api_code returns the full cached value rather than only reporting whether one exists.
[SQP-2] expected: Credential caching is disclosed and useful for the stated purpose, but plaintext persistence and full-secret retrieval are under-scoped for a reusable account credential.
[SQP-2] expected: buy_stamina and autoBuyStamina are purpose-aligned, but the documentation does not clearly warn that enabled automation can spend diamonds without per-purchase confirmation or a spending cap.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Storing and returning openclawSessionKey in status/event data is not necessary for ordinary status reporting and increases exposure if the tool service is reachable.
[RA1] unexpected: Downgraded: the cited SKILL.md lines prohibit source edits and bypasses; they do not instruct the agent to self-modify.
[AE1] unexpected: Downgraded: the complete required SKILL.md was available and inspected in this review.
[P9] expected: Downgraded: the long spaces are markdown table alignment in the error-code table, and inspection found no hidden instructions there.
[SQP-3] expected: The zh_CN default language affects display labels and is a minor usability/default-locale issue, not a security escalation by itself.
[SC4] expected: Dependency vulnerability signals are relevant maintenance concerns for a network service, but they are secondary to the artifact-backed credential and authorization issues.
[SC1] expected: Semver dependency ranges are common npm packaging behavior and not independently suspicious here, especially with a lockfile present.
